title: Escalation path and MSA + escrow onboarding kickoff
summary: Kickoff to align on MSA/DPA redlines, escrow/escrow agent expectations, SLA tiering for latency and uptime, pricing approval path and pilot scope. Customer requires customer-managed keys for PII, SOC2 evidence, and an explicit escalation path for incidents. Agreement to share redline window and schedule security deep dive next week.

DPA details: data residency, retention, deletion timelines
Escrow: code/weights escrow or alternative assurance
SLA: latency targets, credits, regional SLOs
Pricing approvals: reserved capacity vs hosted, egress fees
Security preflight: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, VPC connectivity
Next steps: redline delivery, SOC2 report, pilot run dates

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-17 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Elena Park (Redwood AE), Tom Rivers (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CedarBank Procurement), Marcus Allen (CedarBank Legal), Sophia Li (CedarBank Infra), David Ortiz (CedarBank FinOps)

Summary (auto): Kickoff to align legal/ procurement path for MSA/DPA + escrow, agree a security preflight and pilot scope. Redwood to send documents; customer to return redlines.

[00:00] Elena: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick note, this is a kickoff to map the approval path for CedarBank's onboarding — MSA, DPA, escrow ask, and then the pricing/commit steps. I think we have about 45 minutes, is that right?

[00:14] Priya: Yep that's right, thanks. we'll want to make sure we capture the escalation path, like who to loop in on severity 1 incidents. Also need clarity on the escrow ask - whether Redwood offers model weights escrow or some sort of functional assurance.

[00:28] Tom: (SE) yeah from a technical perspective we can discuss two patterns: dedicated/reserved pools with customer VPC or hosted with private tenancy. For escrow, often customers ask for either source/weights escrow or a contractual SLA backed with operational playbooks. there are tradeoffs on release windows and legal complexity.

[00:45] Marcus: hi, Marcus here. for legal we're focusing on liability cap, indemnity carveouts for third-party models, and termination/transition assistance. if there's an escrow, we need clear access criteria - like what triggers release.

[00:56] Elena: totally. on liability caps we usually see standard limits tied to fees, but for financial customers you flagged you might need a higher cap?

[01:08] David: yeah our finance team will push on that. we need to understand the commercial trade: higher cap vs commitment dollars. currently, the pilot budget is constrained. if there's a reserved capacity commit, we can loosen some terms, but that's what we need to model.

[01:22] Priya: that's helpful. also data residency question — the pilot will be US-only, us-east-1, but the long-term plan could include EU. we need assurances around log retention, deletion timelines in the DPA.

[01:35] Tom: From Redwood side, we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in our private deploy and can do envelope encryption. for hosted we have server-side keys, but we do offer BYOK in Dedicated and Private. caveat: BYOK can introduce some egress and key rotation operational notes.

[01:51] Sophia: can you clarify the KMS flow? like who holds root key and what access Redwood engineering needs for troubleshooting?

[02:05] Tom: yes, so typical pattern: customer holds master key in their KMS; Redwood uses a per-cluster envelope key encrypted by that master. Redwood engineers never see the plaintext master. for debugging we can use audited temporary sessions if needed; those are scope-limited and require your approval (and we log them).

[02:20] Marcus: we will want that audit log detail explicitly in the DPA and the ops playbook. also need SOC2 report and recent pentest summary before procurement signs off.

[02:31] Elena: we'll attach SOC2 Type II and pen test summary. note sometimes the transcriptions show pen test as "pen-test" in docs, but we'll make sure the file names are clear.

[02:40] Priya: thanks. on the escrow topic — is Redwood amenable to a third-party escrow agent holding model artifacts? or do you prefer a contractual fallback?

[02:53] Tom: We've done both. For weights/source escrow we partner with an escrow agent in some enterprise deals; alternatively, we can commit to a robust transition plan with technical handover and a code snapshot under escrow. the legal team typically decides which route.

[03:10] Marcus: okay if you can enumerate options in the MSA addendum that would be ideal. we need to check release triggers e.g., insolvency, failure to provide service for X days, or material breach, and the mechanics to validate integrity of the escrowed artifacts.

[03:30] Elena: action item for us: we'll include two options in the package we send — "weights escrow via third-party agent" and "transition assistance + operational snapshot". we'll flag the downstream requirements and median timelines.

[03:44] David: about SLA: we need region-specific latency SLOs and credit calculation. production needs P95 < 250ms for small prompt flows; is that achievable on dedicated?

[03:58] Tom: on dedicated pools with optimized kernels and persistent batching we can hit sub-200 P95 in us-east for short prompts, yes. hosted tiers are more variable, depends on burst and mixing. we'll include benchmark sheets. note some transcription artifacts might say "P95 200ms" which is shorthand — we'll give the full distribution.

[04:19] Priya: and credits? how are SLA credits applied — offset bill or credit note?

[04:26] Elena: standard is credit applied to invoice; for enterprise we'd be open to discussing contract language that ties credits to future invoices or remediation commitments.

[04:34] Marcus: also need clarity on data deletion: when customer asks for data purge, what's the guaranteed timeline and proof?

[04:44] Tom: we have deletion hooks tied to tenant lifecycle — we can guarantee X days to purge caches, with an audit trail. for retained logs we can set retention windows by agreement. again we will put those terms in the DPA and the operational runbook.

[04:58] Priya: what about egress fees? we read about additional egress fees for heavy embeddings/embeddings storage. can you outline that in pricing?

[05:09] Elena: yes the pricing spreadsheet we'll send will show unit price per 1K tokens for hosted, per-instance hour for dedicated, and any egress/egress-laden storage fees as a separate line. we'll also show an example invoice for the pilot.

[05:23] David: perfect. finance needs that to route approval. we might also need a one-off waiver for a lower liability cap for pilot only, subject to later commit. is that something you can support?

[05:36] Elena: we can propose a pilot-specific clause — limited liability with a short-term cap and a path to increase upon reserved capacity signature. we'll draft that as an option.

[05:47] Marcus: timeline-wise, are you expecting legal to redline this week?

[05:53] Elena: we can publish the canonical MSA/DPA plus the escrow options by 2025-03-19. if you can return redlines by 2025-03-24, we can set a follow-up to sync.

[06:05] Priya: that works. also, can we get a short decision tree for escalations — who do we contact for Sev 1, and what's the expected initial response time?

[06:18] Tom: yes we have an incident escalation playbook: Slack/email pager + 30-min ack for Sev 1 in dedicated tiers, and 60-min for hosted enterprise. we'll send a redacted playbook and propose the names for the escalation points.

[06:33] Sophia: on connectivity: we need an explicit diagram for VPC peering, NAT behaviour, and port list. also, I need to confirm we can use our own proxy for egress controls.

[06:44] Tom: will include a connectivity diagram and port list; BYO-proxy is supported on private deployments. if you want us to run a dry-run connectivity test during pilot, we can schedule that.

[06:57] David: one last item — billing who signs? we have to know whether Procurement or Finance signs OPA/commit. I'll confirm and get back.

[07:06] Elena: great — to recap: Redwood sends docs and SOC2 on 3/19; schedule security deep dive (Tom/Sophia) for next week; Marcus returns redlines by 3/24; David confirms signatory by 3/25.

[07:20] Priya: yep, that captures it. thanks everyone.

[07:24] Marcus: thanks, bye.

(End)
notes: Call recorded via Fireflies. Transcript contains minor mis-hearings (e.g., 'KV cash' for KV cache, 'pen test' sometimes captured as 'pentest').
